concept.name: Trade thesis
concept.definition: A concise, falsifiable statement of why a trade should work: the setup, the edge being exploited, the conditions required, the expected path, and what would prove the idea wrong. It is the pre-committed reasoning against which execution and outcome are later reviewed.
concept.intuition: If you cannot say in two sentences why the trade exists and what kills it, you do not have a trade - you have a hope.
concept.mechanics: Written before entry: context (trend, level, catalyst), the playbook setup, entry trigger, invalidation, target logic, and time frame. It defines in advance the evidence that would disconfirm the idea, anchoring exits to information rather than emotion.
concept.failure_modes: Theses fail when they are unfalsifiable narratives rather than testable claims, or when they are quietly edited after entry as price moves against the position. A coherent story is not an edge - narrative coherence is cheap (narrative bias).
concept.misconceptions: A thesis is not a prediction that must be right; it is a hypothesis with predefined failure conditions. Confidence in the thesis does not substitute for a defined invalidation point.
concept.example: 'Breakout over the three-month range on twice average volume after earnings; invalid below the range top at 102; target the measured move at 115 within two weeks' - every element checkable.
